explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1080 with the answer no. The statement negates the existence of c > 0 such that every bipartite graph on n vertices, with one side (X) of size ⌊n^{2/3}⌋ and at least cn edges, contains a 6-cycle. The de Caen–Székely bound f(n, n^{2/3}) ≫ n^{58/57+o(1)} gives C6-free graphs (in fact {C4,C6}-free) with superlinearly many edges and a part of size about n^{2/3}. Here n counts all vertices rather than one side, which is only a cosmetic difference.
